deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is page 2 of a letter by Karl Hattendorff (signed 'K. Hattendorff' on the next page), filed with Riemann's minimal-surface papers. The letter is probably addressed to Richard Dedekind, since Weber is mentioned in the third person; that addressee is my inference. It concerns the editorial note for 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', the posthumous treatise Hattendorff edited in 1867, as it was being prepared for Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876).

The page gives Hattendorff's account of how the 1867 version of the treatise came about:
(1) In April 1866 Riemann, through (Heinrich) Weber, asked Hattendorff whether he would help write up results Riemann had worked out mentally but was too ill to put on paper himself.
(2) The minimal surfaces were to come first. Riemann expected the job to take about 8 days, after which 'more important things' were to follow.
(3) Riemann had misjudged both the time and his strength. He was often inaccessible for days at a time, could not speak (his voice was toneless, and whispering set off violent coughing), and communicated in writing.
(4) He jotted brief explanations of the manuscript (M.S.) with a stylus on a slate, each time until Hattendorff nodded that he had understood. A few times he wrote in pencil on paper, but always only aphoristically.
(5) The next page continues: between these sessions (rarely longer than half an hour) Hattendorff immediately wrote up what had been worked through, so Riemann saw and approved most of the treatise before leaving for Italy on 16 June 1866.

The previous page dates the original manuscript to 1860–61. It cites two remarks by Riemann: that complex function theory 'admits an interesting application to the minimal surface problem' (said around summer 1861 and no later than summer 1862), and, in April 1866, that the work was already 'five to six years old'.

There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Historical account of how Riemann's minimal-surface treatise was written up by Hattendorff in April–June 1866, through slate and paper notes from the gravely ill Riemann
results.modern_name: Provenance/editorial history of Riemann, 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867)
results.usually_credited_to: Hattendorff's account, essentially as printed in the editorial note of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a non-mathematical editorial letter by Hattendorff, not by Riemann. Its content (the 1860–61 dating and the 1866 write-up under Riemann's illness) is essentially the known story behind the Werke note. The vivid details of slate-and-stylus communication are nice archival color but are not mathematically surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'zur Erläuterung des M. F. dienen sollte' should most likely read 'des M. S.' (Manuscript), consistent with the abbreviation used elsewhere in the letter.
'jedes mal bis ich ihm zunickte[?]': the image supports 'zunickte'; the [?] can be removed.
The text is in Hattendorff's hand (letter), not Riemann's; the folio should be catalogued as editorial correspondence rather than a Riemann working page.
